# Python pass parity

The current reference is `sonolus.py@c45300d46ae53f659d71e0108216e39339434463`
(v1.2.5). `py_current_golden.json` contains its real Cython Standard output for
the same `pipeline_fixture.json`. Generation checks fused and exported emission;
Go checks final memory/effects against all three tiers and the 4096-slot boundary.
This is semantic parity, not a claim of identical private CFGs or runtime cost.

`regenerate.ps1` builds the exact pinned Git archive in an isolated temporary
Python environment (a C compiler is required) and regenerates the current golden.
It prints the retained build environment path. Pass `-Historical` with the old
checkout only when deliberately regenerating the historical snapshots below.

`py_pass_parity_test.go` also consumes historical `py_pass_golden.json`. The snapshot
is generated by the real optimizer in
`sonolus.py@1040bc0dcc116efdbca05f144edec302e839bcd3`.

`pipeline_fixture.json` is the schema v2 neutral CFG input consumed by both
`harness_pipeline.py` and the Go parity test. The generated schema v4 snapshot
records every checkpoint as both canonical text and structured CFG, together with the complete
`STANDARD_PASSES` output, ToSSA, first SCCP cleanup, second SCCP, FromSSA, and
Allocate checkpoints.

The common canonical form uses reverse-postorder block IDs, first-definition
local/SSA versions, predecessor-ordered Phi arguments, and source-order
expression arguments. Every checkpoint is compared structurally. Exact
equivalent differences live in `py_pass_allowlist.json`; unknown and unused
entries fail. Final trees are additionally executed over the fixture input
matrix and compared by semantic memory and ordered effects.

Regenerate the historical snapshot only when deliberately maintaining that baseline:

```powershell
& internal/compiler/testdata/optimize/regenerate.ps1 -Historical -PythonCheckout <historical-checkout>
```

Normal Go tests only consume the checked-in snapshot and do not require Python
or an adjacent checkout.
